issue: Does the rule in Honeycutt v. United States, barring joint and several liability for forfeiture of tainted property, apply to forfeiture under 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C)?

sides.position: Honeycutt applies to 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C), because the text and structure of § 981 are substantially the same as the statute in Honeycutt, so joint and several forfeiture liability is barred.
cases: United States v. Gjeli, 867 F.3d 418 (3d Cir. 2017)
United States v. Thompson, 990 F.3d 680 (9th Cir. 2021)

sides.position: Honeycutt does not apply to 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C), because that provision does not limit forfeiture to proceeds the person obtained, so property need only be traceable to the crime, not received by the forfeiting defendant.

this_court: Honeycutt applies to 18 U.S.C. § 981(a)(1)(C), agreeing with the Third Circuit.
quote: Our sister circuits are split on whether Honeycutt applies to 18 U.S.C. § 981.
cite: United States v. Vassily Thompson, 990 F.3d 680 (9th Cir. 2021)
